Job's simple. Get into warehouse (coordinates attached), steal the security cam footage and bring it back to Aaron. Should be enough to push his case through. And if you happen to shoot a few Maelstromers along the way, well... shit happens, right? World won't be worse off without them, that's for sure.

options.text: Turns out things are a little more complicated than at first glance. McCarlson isn't running an investigation – he's tryna cover up his tracks. Watch the recording.

messages.text: Got the recording along with the news that Aaron's dead. Pretty unprofessional, but... fuck it, I might've gone and done the same. The things you see in this fucking city...

V, I… I understand your decision, but you could've handled that differently. Aaron was a bastard, but a bastard with influence. And you had dirt on him. But what's done is done. Our client's dead and gone which means so's our payment – you understand. Gig shut and forgotten.

Ugh... Well, this situation took a rough turn. But thanks for a job well done, V. And don't worry about Aaron. Let him sleep it off. When he wakes up, he'll remember we have the recording, and then, well… Then we've got our own inside source at the NCPD. Gig shut and sealed.
Aaron's happy. I'm happy. Always pays to be on good terms with badges, right? Gig's closed, eddies on their way.

title: Malware from b@d
text:
Regina Jones: Gig type: Agent Saboteur
Objective: Upload b@d's malware
Location: Megabuilding H11
Details:

b@d got in touch with me. They like short nicknames and simple gigs, so I'll spare you the fixer spiel and get right to the point.

You'll find b@d's malware attached to this message. You have to download it (just be careful – it's hella dangerous) and then upload it to the subnet in the H11 megabuilding. Piece o' cake, right? Sorry to burst your bubble, but you'll have Tygers on the prowl.

b@d's plan is to attack some Arasaka subnet and use H11 as a smokescreen. Clever, right? Instead of leading to them, all traces of b@d's breach'll lead right back to the megabuilding.

FYI, our netrunner already hacked the megabuilding elevator, so getting into the server room won't be a problem.
Regina Jones: b@d's happy, which means I'm happy, which means you get your eddies and everyone's happy! Contract closed. Thanks, V!

title: Glitter
text:
Regina Jones: Gig type: Agent Saboteur
Objective: Destroy the glitter lab
Location: Building on Rovinj St.
Details

Unless you've been living under a rock, you've heard of Glitter. Word is that if you take it, you're hooked for life, but apparently it's easier to OD on than neo-fentanyl.

It was only a matter of time before some zit-faced, rich kid fried his skull sponge. Kid's mother was Arati Kapoor, co-owner of the Masala Studios restaurant franchise. Needless to say, she's pretty torn up about it, but she's not the kind to wallow in her grief – she's got a plan.

The lab where glitter is cooked has to be wiped off the face of the earth. And if some of those dipshits making it expire on the spot? I think you know the answer.

Flicking you the coords now. FYI – the place might be guarded by Tyger Claws.
Regina Jones: Poof! No more lab! Just like the doctor ordered. 'Course, let's not kid ourselves. Glitter's here to stay. But at least we hit the fuckers makin' it right where it hurts. Oh, one last thing – Arati asked me to thank you for her, said she's very grateful. So, thanks. Catch you later.

title: Cyberpsychosis Investigation
text:
Regina Jones: V! WAIT! Are you jacked into the NCPD scanner? You took that cyberpsychosis hustle, right? If you did, I want to make you an offer. Once the job's done, put your nose to the ground and try to figure out what exactly went down. If you find anything that could shed light on the matter, send the files over to me. In return I'll cut through all the NCPD red tape and make sure they send the money over to you stat.
Regina Jones: You're probably wondering why this is any of my concern. Here's the truth – this "cyberpsychosis" epidemic's really getting under my skin. The number of incidents is way too high. I'm getting that tingling from back in my media days – something just doesn't add up. I wanna find out what's causing these outbreaks and who's responsible for them. I don't buy the story that it's because of "too many implants" – it doesn't make any sense. There's gotta be another explanation.
Regina Jones: If you're thinking about trying to help those people who've got hustles out on them – don't. It's too late – you won't get through to them. Still, there's always more than meets the eye about all these cases. If we put all the pieces together and find out what's causing cyberpsychosis, maybe we can find a way to get rid of it once and for all. Let's stay in touch, V.

title: Cyberpsycho Sighting: Lt. Mower
text:
V [choice]: Hey, sending you the data I got from the Militech woman. Turns out she was in the corp's special unit. Clearly, she felt something was seriously wrong and put out a call for help. But instead of help, Militech sent in a hit squad...
Regina Jones: Preem, sending you a ride. I managed to extract some more data about her, but not much. You know how it is with Militech – get too nosey and they start sending you death threats. Looks like Mower was chipped with experimental combat implants. Maybe there was some glitch in the code that made her snap? I'll look into it. Thanks again – money's already on its way.
Regina Jones: OK, so all I know is that a cyberpsycho attack was reported to MaxTac, but Militech elbowed in and took over, probably because it was one of their own – a woman named Mower serving in Militech's elite division. Be careful, all right?
V [choice]: Hey, got some info on Mower. Turns out she used to be Militech spec ops. She was feeling seriously off and called the corp to send help. They sent a fire squad instead… Listen, she didn't make it but that's cuz self-defense was my only choice.
Regina Jones: It's too bad you had to kill her. Mower was chipped with experimental combat implants. Who knows, maybe she had a glitch in her system – something we could've found to help her. Oh well... Sending your fee, but next time I'd appreciate some effort on your part.
Regina Jones: Got word of a cyberpsycho attack, all confirmed. Even reported to MaxTac. Thing is, nobody's gonna show cause Militech shut it right down. Psycho's gotta be one of theirs. My eddies are on Lieutenant Mower. Anyway, corpo's gonna go straight into treatment. So make very, very sure you keep her in one piece.

title: Cyberpsycho Sighting: Demons of War
text:
Regina Jones: If he zeroed the badges then there's no way in hell MaxTac is gonna bring him in alive. We're the best chance he's got at getting out of this in one piece.
V [choice]: Our psycho's out cold, but alive. Transferring you the data I gathered. Looks like it was an ex-merc working for some corp. Soon as he stopped being useful, they tossed him out on the street. Guy kept his combat implants, had PTSD, stopped taking his meds... You can fill in the blanks.
Regina Jones: Thanks for going the extra mile. So a badge friend of mine just sent over his data. Guy's head was a mess – must've taken 4x doses just to make it through the day. Eventually the corp cut off his health insurance, the cash dried up, and then the ticking time bomb exploded. But was it really from the implants alone? Who the hell knows. Either way, your eddies are in the air. Thanks for taking care of this.
V [choice]: Perp's flatlined. Looks like our guy was a merc on a corpo contract. After he outlived his usefulness, he hit the streets – combat implants still intact. Combine that with homelessness, PTSD and not taking anti-psycho meds... You can picture the rest.
Regina Jones: Shame you didn't try to save him. Badge friend of mine sent me his spec – guy's head was a mess, must've been taking 4x doses to make it through the day. Corp cut off his health insurance, cash dried up, ticking time bomb exploded. Maybe if he'd just gone back on his meds, things could've ended happily ever after.

title: Cyberpsycho Sighting: Six Feet Under
text:
Regina Jones: I'm not seeing any other gang activity around the bridge so we can safely rule out any score-settling. Seems to me one of the Maelstromers just had a bad day or dialed his implants a little too high – hard to tell when it comes to them. All I know is the rest showed up at the wrong time and a bloodbath ensued. I'm betting on cyberpsychosis – even Maelstrom's harshest welcomes don't come close to this.
V [choice]: Our kid was a Valentino, not a Maelstromer. Borg fiends must've had an axe to grind with him, cause they stuffed him with implants like a fucking Christmas turkey and just watched and waited for him to blow. Same would happen to anyone chipped that fast. Body didn't have time to adjust to the 'ware and turned him psycho. Good thing he still had a little self-control left – meant I could take him down quietly.
V [choice]: Our kid was a Valentino, not a Maelstromer. Borg fiends must've had an axe to grind with him, cause they stuffed him with implants like a fucking Christmas turkey and just watched and waited for him to blow. Same would've happened to anyone chipped that fast. Body didn't have time to adjust to the 'ware and turned him psycho. Couldn't bring him in quietly – had to put him outta his misery.
Regina Jones: Looks like our guy didn't even have to piss them off. While ago Maelstrom put out word it was looking for volunteers to test some new 'ware – obviously nobody stepped up so the borg-fucks just started scooping peeps up off the street. Valentinos been looking for this kid for a while, not to mention the runner who swarmed the net with data-feelers trying to track him down. Eventually must've broken free and fought for his life, made the Maelstromers reaped what they sowed. Whole thing backfired on them spectacularly. Good thing you managed to get him to go down softly. Kid's still young, maybe with the right kind of help he can learn to adapt to his new... condition.

title: Cyberpsycho Sighting: Ticket to the Major Leagues
text:
Regina Jones: One more thing – the security in these places is always beefed up, so chances our guy's gonna pack a heavy punch.
V [choice]: Uncovered a smalltime drug ring at the port with buffet-style variety in what they were pushing. Folks buying it are mostly the local have-nots, and the rate of cyberpsychotic breaks among them is on the rise. I think what we're seeing is a connection driven by the new drug cocktail that's making waves. Got the guy sleeping soundly over here, won't be up any time soon. Ready for pickup. Guessing labwork should show you what kinda crap he's got swimming around in his bloodstream.
Regina Jones: Great, appreciate the heads-up. Corps don't like getting their hands dirty with people living on curb level, but when a dealer mixes glitter with coal dust or some other shit they get eddie signs in their eyes. The money still lands in their pockets and another bunch of the city's "undesirables" fades from the streets forever. Win-win...
Regina Jones: Thanks for the info. Shame our guy had to die. Corps don't like getting their hands dirty – AKA cutting deals with street scum. But hey, if a dealer mixing glitter with charcoal or some shit can increase their profit margins? By all fucking means! Even better if a few gonks get zeroed in the process – less dirt on the streets
Sorry for the rant – I've had it up to here with this shit. He was just another merc like you, except his luck ran out.
V [choice]: Just so happens I found a little drug hustle going on at the port – a colorful assortment of to boot. Customers are mostly just poor locals. Got word a bunch of them are showing cyberpsychosis symptoms, and I'm thinking it's no coincidence that the latest drug-blend to make the rounds is a hit. Unfortunately you won't be taking any samples, because I already offed the supplier. All I can say is that the biggest buyers are usually heavily chipped and can't afford painkillers or implant-adapting meds, which means the ingredients are probably similar.

title: Cyberpsycho Sighting: Under the Bridge
text:
Regina Jones: If this is a cyberpsycho it's pretty damn odd. Could be a netrunner - can't quite rule out a remote attack. Still… what would they be looking for in an Arroyo bum camp? Something's off here. Pop over and check it out.
V [choice]: Psycho was a young runner. Think she must've OD'd then ducked outside at the last minute, afraid she'd be left to rot all alone. One of the bums from the camp took her in but when she woke up her mind was cracked. Guess she thought they kidnapped her. Who knows, maybe there wasn't a thought at all tween her ears - just a droning buzz. But anyway, she's awaits your mystery "treatment."
V [choice]: Psycho was a young runner looking for her input who vanished somewhere. Had herself convinced he was kidnapped but never got answers to the "who"or "why." She was hoping one more day in the Net would dig up the trail she needed. Days turned to weeks and she drowned in the digital ether. I didn't manage to salvage what little was left of her. Had no choice but to end her suffering or she'd have ended mine.
Regina Jones: It won't be easy to reverse what she went through, but I'm glad you didn't kill her nonetheless. With the right care she might just get back up on her feet.
Regina Jones: There's no way this ever ended well. Even if they did reunite it wouldn't be with their old selves.

text:

title: Cyberpsycho Sighting: Letter of the Law
text:
Regina Jones: Got noises coming from an auto shop, sounded like a series of explosions. My take – either the roof collapsed, or someone's gone cyberpsycho.
V [choice]: Autoshop owner was on a rampage – but I managed to put him to sleep.
Regina Jones: The way corps here gobble up small businesses... it's almost painful to watch. Before they even clock what's happening, the owners are locked out of their own premises and slapped with a colossal debt. Then they bust their asses for the corp from morning to midnight to make ends meet. Looks like this one preferred to take his own life than give up the one place that was his. See how quickly the American dream can turn into the American nightmare?

title: Cyberpsycho Sighting: Seaside Cafe
text:
Regina Jones: A popular cafe with a beautiful view of the ocean, usually crowded at this hour. It acquired cult notoriety after Saigon Sisters was filmed there, and it's Hyunh's favorite eatery. Poor thing, lying in a coma after an allergic reaction to tannins... Anyway, cafe's booked now for some bougie reception. Few of the guests already arrived and the newlyweds were getting their stills taken – that's when it all started. Guess someone seriously objected to this holy matrimony...
V [choice]: You're right, it's a reality TV show. Watson Whore doesn't even compare
Regina Jones: Glad she's alive. Maybe there's a chance she'll start telling apart real life from TV life so we can start helping her. I'm just worried what'll happen when she finally realizes that massacre wasn't fake blood and artificial limbs.
Regina Jones: Sucks pretty damn hard you couldn't save her. Maybe if she could've separated the real world from her TV life, we would've stood a better chance of helping her. Sadly for her, she didn't just die a TV death this time.
Regina Jones: Get a load of this. It wasn't an actual wedding – it was supposed to be an episode for your favorite TV show, Saigon Sisters. Spoilers incoming. The plan was to pit both sisters against each other by chipping one with faulty implants and putting her in a coma (not from an allergic reaction, but with legit poison). In the meantime, the other sister gets plastic surgery to look like the sister in a coma so she can marry the latter's fiance. How whacked is that? Except the coma-sister woke up too soon, forgot she was on a TV show, and clearly didn't like her new implants – a fact she made known at the wedding reception with a performance no one would forget... at least, for the ones that managed to escape. First she took care of her sister, then the husband, and finally the whole TV crew – that's when guts really hit the fan. I thought Maelstrom were fucked up, but showbiz takes the cake this time.
V [choice]: Got some good news – there's a happy ending to your favorite TV show after all. Our psycho-star's alive and well. Flicking you the detes.
V [choice]: Got some bad news – turns out there's no happy ending for your favorite TV show. Our psycho reality star's dead. Flicking you the detes.
Regina Jones: V, listen. A gunfight broke out in a cafe on the waterfront. See what's goin on over there, k? If it's a cyberpsycho problem, I want that problem to stay alive.

text:
Regina Jones: He's outfitted in full military gear, so he could be a vet suffering from PTSD... but why the getup? Maybe he felt the cyberpsychosis coming on and wanted to look the part? Something doesn't add up…
V [choice]: Gangers picked the wrong choom to fuck with.
Regina Jones: Tygers took a liking to the girl and decided to turn her into a doll. Big mistake. LIttle did they know her daddy was ex special forces - wasted no time in hunting their sorry hides down. Only option they had left was to lure him into a trap. Bigger mistake. Don't underestimate an ex commando who wants his daughter back - he hunted every last Tyger as easily as if he was on a goddamn safari.
Regina Jones: Glad you made it out in one piece and left our guy alive. Too bad NC's apex predators already sniffed him out - meaning MaxTac. Probably best if we get out of their way this time.
Regina Jones: Glad you made it out in one piece. Our guy put up a hell of a fight, so there was nothing left to do but defend yourself.
V [choice]: Wasn't easy, but I managed to keep him alive.
V [choice]: Couldn't get close to him - put up a hell of a fight. Left me no choice - had to zero him.
Regina Jones: V, got a hot gig. Some soldier just opened fire on pedestrians at the pier. Try and grab him for me, alive. If you can't, well... at least give it a try. Then I'll send the right people for him. Good luck.

title: Cyberpsycho Sighting: Discount Doc
text:
Regina Jones: One of the workers went psycho, started smashing up the construction site. Seems some of the workers tried to stop him, but their little poly one-shots couldn't pierce that exoskeleton of his. Anyway, they either ran or got added to the construction, if you catch my drift. Go check it out for me.
V [choice]: Guess even pneumatic arms can't lift morale in a toxic workplace.
Regina Jones: My, my, now that's some creative management. Seems this developer has no problem creating a wide range of business needs and solutions. I'm sure his long-standing connections with weapons dealers, the NCPD and other shady souls help enormously. And if a certain need isn't great enough, well, there's always the usual solutions of arm-twisting and kneecapping. The key to success remains flexibility, especially of the moral sort.
Regina Jones: Really glad you got him alive. Poor guy almost completely spiraled out before he even realized what was happening.

title: Cars for sale
text:
Regina Jones: Hello, V. I have a Makigai MaiMai for sale. Aside from sounding like a fruity cocktail, it is a little small – but you, your guns and your groceries will fit right in. What more do you need?
Regina Jones: Hi, V! Got a Quartz waiting to be checked out. Fine machine, well taken care of, polished to a shine. Bought it off a certain gentleman who was a little whacked when it came to his car, huffing and puffing in his garage day in, day out. Until, that is, his wife filed for divorce – the ride had to go to pay the legal fees. Lemme know if you're interested.
Regina Jones: Hey! Letting you know I got a reeeally nice Thorton Colby for sale. Belonged to some car-jacker from Memphis, a certain Nicholas, may he rest in peace. He'd klep the most expensive wheels for rich buyers – you know, Rayfields, Herreras – but for years he always drove this Colby. I'd tell you why, but you'll know for yourself the second you get behind the wheel.
Regina Jones: Hey hey, there's a Mizutani Shion that's looking for a new home. Won't lie, might be a little beaten up. Previous chick who owned it liked to lead-foot the pedal, but the engine, suspension, brakes, everything that matters – all that's in preem condish. Rides like a pure dream. This baby's a classic, and a fast one at that – perfect for losing the 5-0. Oh, and the flooring might be a little stained. Coffee...? Blood? Hard to tell.
Regina Jones: V, my favorite merc! I got a Galena I'm selling. Hasn't been driven much – guy who owned for the last ten years was paranoid as shit of going outside cuz he was afraid "they" would zero him – car sat unloved for all that time. But you can't escape fate, right? Stray lead caught him through his window. Moral of the story's that you gotta grab life by the fucking balls. So don't be no scrooge, whip out your credchip and buy this baby.
Regina Jones: I knew I could tempt you :) Enjoy it!
Regina Jones: Good luck with it, V. And watch out for the NCPD – nothing they love better than writing up tickets.
Regina Jones: Hey, so the "Cthulhu" has just emerged from the abyss. Sounds scary, right? Seriously though – car's out of this fucking world. Barely even touch the gas and next thing you know you're burning rubber and your eyes are tearing up. Long story short, it's not for everyone. But something tells me if anyone can handle this beast, it's you. Buy it and don't look back.

title: Cyberpsycho Research
text:
Regina Jones: Hey V, you know that cyberpsychosis research you've been helpin me with? Well, thought you might be interested to hear some of the initial findings. Bad news first - looks like there's no saving most of these patients. But there's a glimmer of hope - in one case the delusions disappeared almost completely. It's still unclear whether this was the result of pharmaceutical therapy, psychotherapy or some combination of both. I'm not ready to call this a breakthrough just yet but... I do think we've at least taken a first step forward in learning how to help these people. Thank you, V. And kudos.
Regina Jones: V, got a job opp for ya. I won't sugarcoat it, it's a risky one. You'd be breaking into a Maelstrom den. Reach out if you're interested.

title: About Skippy
text:
Regina Jones: Hey V, got some news about Skippy, our chatty little choom with the moody trigger. I had a visit with the techie who created him (and lost him in a card game).
Regina Jones: He's had a hot hand at the tables lately, so he came by with the cash to buy his buddy back. Not the whole gun, mind you. Just the AI component.
Regina Jones: Anyway, thought maybe you might want what's left? (the gun I mean, without the AI). I get the feeling you can be the sentimental type, so maybe you'll want it as a keepsake. If you're interested, you can pick it up at my place, near the elevator. Cheers.

title: NCPD Dispatch
text:
NCPD Dispatcher: Calling all NCPD subcons. Suspected organized crime activity reported on Carnitas Street. Sixth Street Gang has established a presence led by Olga Elizabeth Longmead, wanted for kidnapping and first-degree murder, two counts. NC authorities have posted a reward for neutralizing the threat in that area.
NCPD Dispatcher: To all NCPD subcons – suspected organized crime activity reported near intersection of Sequoia and Gray. APB out on Paul Craven. Priors include corporate convoy hijacking. Also a known leader within an NC human trafficking ring. Active affiliations include the Wraiths gang. City authorities have offered a reward for neutralizing the threat.
NCPD Dispatcher: APB to all NCPD subcons. Suspected organized crime activity reported on Pacific Boulevard. Anton Kolev, a known leader among scavengers, believed to be present and wanted on four counts of first-degree murder. Night City authorities have promised a reward for neutralizing Kolev and his entourage.
NCPD Dispatcher: Attention all NCPD subcons. Suspected organized crime activity reported around Eden Beach Mega Ride. Stanislaus Zbyszko likely at the scene. Perp is a known captain among scavengers with multiple smuggling priors. City authorities have a reward on offer for neutralizing Zbyszko and his group.
NCPD Dispatcher: Calling all NCPD subcons. Suspected organized crime activity reported on Skyline South. Group of Valentinos led by Zoe Alonzo at large. Her record includes armed robbery, extortion, kidnapping and first-degree murder. Night City authorities offering a reward for neutralizing Alonzo's criminal network.
NCPD Dispatcher: Calling all NCPD subcons. Suspected organized crime activity reported on Martin Luther King Boulevard. Members of the Valentinos engaged in smuggling and trafficking operations. Group is led by Miguel Rodriguez, AKA "Gizmo." Priors include second-degree murder and drug trafficking. City's put out a reward for neutralizing the threat.
NCPD Dispatcher: Calling all NCPD subcons. APB out on suspected organized crime activity over on Sycamore Street. Due to nonpayment of rent and related fees, Night City has terminated its lease agreement with Impala Automatics for industrial property owned by the city. Impala Automatics has failed to comply with the decision and now illegally occupies the premises specified in the contract. City authorities have offered a reward for the successful eviction of Impala Automatics.
NCPD Dispatcher: Calling all NCPD subcons. Suspected organized crime activity observed in the region of Goldsmith Street. Scavenger presence reported, led by one Barry Alken, wanted on charges of first-degree murder and illegal trade in cyberware. NC authorities offering payment for neutralizing Alken and his accomplices.
NCPD Dispatcher: Attention all NCPD subcons. Suspected organized crime activity reported at corner of Drake and Cartwright. Tyger Claw gang members suspected of armed robbery and extortion are at the scene. Leader is Mokomichi Yamada, AKA "Motor Boy." City's put up a reward for the removal of Yamada and his accomplices from the area.
NCPD Dispatcher: Attention all NCPD subcons – suspected organized crime activity reported off Willow Street. APB out on one Shinobu Imai, convicted on multiple counts of human trafficking and forced labor. City officials offering a reward for neutralizing Imai's criminal network in the Willow Street area.
NCPD Dispatcher: Attention all NCPD subcons. Suspected organized crime activity reported near I-9. Perps in question tied to a series of robberies in the Badlands. Group is led by Bruce Ward, affiliated with the so-called Wraiths gang. NC authorities have offered a reward for neutralizing the threat.
NCPD Dispatcher: Attention all NCPD subcons. Suspected organized crime activity reported on Sage Gulch Road. Warrants issued for Rufus McBride on counts of practicing as a ripperdoc without a license. Record shows three counts of causing permanent disabilty and one count of aiding in the staging of a suicide. Perp is in hiding among members of the Wraiths gang. City is offering a reward for neutralizing the threat and the group concealing him.
NCPD Dispatcher: All NCPD subcons – APB out for suspect accused of organized crime activity near Ross Street and Shipyard Way. Scavengers led by Yelena Sidorova – presumed to be armed and dangerous – have assaulted multiple homeless persons. Night City officials are offering a reward for neutralizing the threat.
NCPD Dispatcher: Calling all NCPD subcons. Suspected organized crime activity reported over on Richmond Street. Intel indicates Maelstrom gang members dealing in illegal stimulants in the area. They're led by Tom Ayer, AKA "Ymir", a known serial killer. Night City authorities have offered a reward for neutralizing the group.
NCPD Dispatcher: Attention all NCPD subcons – organized crime activity reported on Martin Street. Maelstrom has established a presence in the area. Kaiser Herzog, AKA "The Surgeon," spotted. Priors include practicing as a ripperdoc without a license and first-degree murder, for which he has been sentenced to death. City authorities are offering a reward for the removal of Herzog and Maelstrom from the area.

title: Just airing my dirty laundry...
text:
Panam Palmer: OK, I can't stop thinking about this, so I'm just going to unload it on you and you can ignore it if you wish. I've had it up to HERE with Saul! Does he TRULY think this family will be better off by selling its soul to a corp? I've never seen someone with their head so far up their ass. Nothing about this is going to end well...
V [choice]: Now don't get mad, BUT maybe dealin with those corpos ain't the worst thing? Gettin along alright with one myself - Takemura, pretty chill and honorable choom. Not all corps are monoliths. Some of their peeps can be decent too.
V [choice]: Got no love for corpos either. And I prolly have more reason than you. Had the displeasure to meet one recently - Takemura. Slimy fucker like the rest, mouth full of platitudes. So trust me when I say I hear you…
V [choice]: Preachin to the choir – Arasaka chewed me up and spat me out soon as I stopped being useful... That said, recently met this suit Takemura, worked for Saburo. Pretty decent choom, led by honor, not self interest. Defy expectations sometimes, these corpos...
Panam Palmer: V, listen to me – working at a megacorp isn't a job like any other, it's an identity. I don't trust them and frankly, anyone who deals with them is asking for trouble. Just be careful, all right? Oh, and thanks, by the way. I stopped thinking about Saul and started thinking about you – much more pleasant ;)
V [choice]: Glad to hear it... :) On the subject of Takemura, I get what you're saying, but I think he really might be cut from a different cloth. I can't really explain it. As for Saul, just follow your instinct. It's what you do best ;)
V [choice]: Anytime ;) I guess you're right about corpos... I have no way of really knowing if Takemura's hiding something or scheming. But you know, with my luck, I'll probably find out soon enough...
V [choice]: Yeah... Worst part is you never know what's riskier – dealing with corps or turning your back on them, especially when you're on your own :/ Look out for yourselves, OK? Probably better to keep a close eye on Saul...
Panam Palmer: Thanks... Somehow I feel a little better already. It's as if talking to you has somehow unclouded my head. If I know one thing, it's that the Aldecaldos joining up with a corp can only end badly. I feel it in my gut. Hang in there, V ;)

title: Heeey, V! :*
text:
Panam Palmer: Listen, I can't stop thinking about what we discussed earlier... the chip and, well... how did all that even happen? (No need to answer if you don't want to!)
V [choice]: I hope I'll get a chance to tell you the whole story, unfiltered, but basically... I was part of a crew in Night City. We wanted to make something of ourselves, have everyone at the Afterlife kissing the ground we walked on and not have to worry about next month's rent. This one fixer offered us a heap of eddies to steal the biochip from Arasaka. What could possibly go wrong, we figured...
Panam Palmer: Jesus Christ, V... I'm so sorry :( I know this will come as little comfort, but... I get the feeling the V you're talking about no longer exists. The V I know isn't in it for the fame, or money... That's not the V that would sit by the campfire with me and gaze up at the stars. What I'm trying to say is – you've changed, and everything that meant something before means something different now.
V [choice]: I hope you won't see me differently for saying this, but I'm not done showing this city what I'm made of – even if all I can muster up is a big ol' fuck you...

title: Truck full of goodies
text:
Mr. Hands: Gig type: Thievery
Objective: Steal a van hauling the Animals' medical supplies
Location: Baptiste St.
Details:

Here's the situation, you need to enter an Animal den steal a certain van carrying medical stimulants. A modified lidocaine, to be precise.

Keep in mind the cargo is rather hot – stolen already once before from Maelstrom.

Those metalmongers use the lidocaine for initation rites, whereas the intend to use it as an ingredient in their favorite "juice" cocktail. In my line of work, we call this a market shortage. What do you say we up the demand even more?

Step 1 - you steal the van. Step 2 – I resell the lidocaine to ripperdoc., Step 3 – they sell it at market price. Step 4 – profit.
Mr. Hands: You just raked in a hefty heap of eddies and have those Animals seein' red. See, I like folks who know how to leave a lasting impression. Think I'll close this contract and hold onto your number for a while.
Mr. Hands: Hear that? It's the sound of a slow clap for the spectacular mess you made. That car was worth quite a sum, and since "someone" went and totaled it – that someone won't be getting paid for their work.

I’ve just spoken with our client. She had some choice words for me for, as she put it, “leaving her in the fucking lurch,” after which the call was dropped. Would you care to explain this state of affairs, V?

options.text: Something came up, something urgent. I don’t leave gigs on a whim.
Whole gig stunk from a mile away, Hands. Know what I’m doing.

messages.text: I see. Interesting.

If you’d be so kind as to take some time out of your busy schedule, there’s a job. Your client's Bree Whitney, journalist. She says she has corporats on her tail and needs help, yet declines to provide further details. Before you meet with her, take the access card from her apartment: 18 Skyline West, fifth floor, last door on the right. The card's in a safebox under a bamboo plant. Write to me, please, once you have it.

title: Dogtown biz
text:
Mr. Hands: By some miracle, it seems Jago and Bennett are now working in tandem. I have no idea how you did it, but Dogtown has never been this well-run. Truly excellent work.
Mr. Hands: I will say, Jago’s influence is sorely missed. Certain items of business must be dealt with on the fly. However, Bennett has risen to the occasion, maintained peace and a... well, let’s call it an organized consensus. All things being said, a smooth transfer of power if there ever was one. Well done, V.
Mr. Hands: Well, well, just a few days and Bennett is no longer missed. Jago’s managing better than I expected - it seems you bet on the right hound. Of course, some scavengers have yet to accept the result and will insist on making trouble... but, well they’re scavengers, not a chess club. Scavengers and trouble go hand in hand.
Mr. Hands: Stop by Heavy Hearts, please. There’s a job, an important and (need I say it?) lucrative one. I trust you won’t be disappointed.
Mr. Hands: Once you’re finished with a certain DA, pay me a visit, please. I’ve got an urgent job that’s best discussed face-to-face and completed quickly.
Mr. Hands: It seems we’ve made the correct choice. Bennett is already cleaning up Dogtown, starting with the Voodoo Boys and the scavengers. Dogtown’s population is down eighteen since yesterday – quite a few eggs to crack, though I’m sure the resulting omelet will be well worth the effort. All in all, we’re on the right track. You can see it yourself, can’t you, V?
Mr. Hands: I have to hand it to you, V. Do you know who just stopped by my office for a cup of tea and a chat? Jago, Dogtown’s new top dog. He wished to discuss a few items of district business. An attitude like that bodes well for the future. It’s best to get along with one’s neighbors, don’t you think? Together, I believe we can bring order back to Dogtown, and neither Bennett nor his current associates can stand in our way.
Mr. Hands: I assume you’re an interested party – Kurt Hansen has given up the ghost while in the hospital. Unsurprisingly, all the hospital cameras malfunctioned at once, while the security guard went out for a smoke. In my professional opinion, someone took advantage of the situation, whether it was one of BARGHEST’s many competitors, an ambitious underling or an unhappy client – the exact party is immaterial. I’d urge caution, especially at this time, V. Hounds unleashed tend to bite.
Mr. Hands: It seems someone rebranded the stadium and lived to tell the tale. My congratulations to them, whoever they may be. In worse news, Kurt Hansen caught the proverbial stray bullet. He’s dead. Whether it was his competition or some ambitious underling, an unknown someone sensed the opportunity and fired. I do know what his death spells for Dogtown – trouble. I’ll be in touch soon.
Mr. Hands: Care for some advice? Caution, V, especially now. After the untimely death of their master, Hansen’s hounds will be tearing at each other’s throats – and at any outsiders who get in their way.

title: Family Matters at Heavy Hearts
text:
Mr. Hands: Gig objective: Complete assignment from Michael Maldonado

Location: Golden Pacific

Details: I have been informed that this is a delicate matter, however mundane it may be. Michael Maldonado has been blessed with two things: a wayward son and endless trouble. He will inform you of the exact nature of the assistance he requires. All I know is Michael is willing to compensate you – and me – surprisingly well for our efforts.

Visit him to learn more about the nature of the job. Maldonado runs a business that he never seems to leave. You know how it is, V – those with the least stand to lose the most.
Mr. Hands: It seems Michael Maldonado expected things to turn out differently. Given that he has failed to provide any details on the matter, I leave that cross for him to bear.
Mr. Hands: It seems Michael Maldonado expected things to turn out differently. Given that he has failed to provide any details on the matter, I leave that cross for him to bear.
Mr. Hands: Michael Maldonado had nothing but praise for you. I hope the feeling is mutual and the contract was smooth sailing.
Mr. Hands: Michael Maldonado had nothing but praise for you. I hope the feeling is mutual and the contract was smooth sailing.
Mr. Hands: Michael has informed me you’ll be visiting the Heavy Hearts to deal with his business. I would only remind you it is my place of business as well, so abstain from the usual ruckus and handle things discreetly, please.
Mr. Hands: V. With all of Dogtown at stake, Maldonado’s little gig can wait. Please, first solve the issue of Hansen’s successor.
Mr. Hands: Dogtown’s future is secure; Aguilar has left the district. Let us return to other, less pressing items of business. Such as the job you received from Michael Maldonado.

Mr. Hands: Well, what matters is you acted with discretion. Closing the gig.
Mr. Hands: You did indeed. And quietly, too, for which I’m grateful. Contract closed.
Mr. Hands: Wonderful to hear.

Mr. Hands: I’ll leave your financial arrangements between the two of you, V. However, I believe I requested discretion. Following your decidedly indiscreet behavior in Heavy Hearts, I’ll be cleaning up my affairs with BARGHEST for some time. Contract closed.

title: Dogtown’s Wild World of Sports
text:
Mr. Hands: Gig objective: Acquire Fiona Vargas's client data

Location: Center for Neuromotor Development, Site 341 in Luxor Heights

Details: Can you believe some people avoid paying their taxes? Shocking, I know. Someone needs to put a stop to it. Who is guilty of such heinous crimes, you might ask? Sports scouts who fly in from all across the globe to the center run by Fiona Vargas. They sign contracts with promising athletes, wire sizeable transfers and dodge taxes while they're at it. Our client isn't thrilled.

You'll be acquiring any data linked to Fiona's clients and their contracts. Getting in won't be easy, which is why you'll have the help of my netrunner near the site. Best of luck, V.
Mr. Hands: Data received. It’s time you made your exit.
V [choice]: You know they were chippin’ kids in there?
V [choice]: Who cares so much about taxes?
Mr. Hands: Why so dramatic? It's an open secret by now; everyone knows, few care. If I've offended your sense of moral decency, I do apologize. Until next time, V.
Mr. Hands: I’ve sent the data I received to our client. However, I must say: I expected the client roster to be longer and include, well, some heavier hitters. Nobody likes a lightweight, V. Contract closed.
Mr. Hands: Nicely done, V. Thanks to you, our Europeans can make sure tax evaders meet their punishment. Contract closed.
Mr. Hands: The EEC only wants what it is owed. As they pay well, I'm only happy to oblige. Until our next contract, V.

title: Little Miss Terrorist
text:
Mr. Hands: Gig objective: Thwart a terrorist attack

Location: Weapons factory on the top level of the stadium

Details: If there’s one thing terrorists like, it’s setting off bombs, but Crimson Harvest really seems to have a blast. They’ve already got several successful operations to their name – that is, if you were to ask them. Biotechnica wouldn’t consider the loss of its top employees anything but a failure.

I can't say for sure what Nele Springer is up to, but it seems she’s grown tired of her role in Crimson Harvest. She seems stressed, and it’s hard to blame her. You don’t just up and leave a terrorist cell, do you? Meet with her at the stadium, please, to discuss the details.
Mr. Hands: As always, I appreciate the professionalism, V. In your line of business, passing judgement is much like passing gas in company – it may offer temporary relief, but people will turn their backs on you soon enough. Your job here is done.
Mr. Hands: Perhaps I didn't make myself clear. In the future, remember one little rule: the client is always right. If you'd like to take the moral high ground, please do so on your own time and with your own money. I trust that's clear enough. Your gig is complete.
V [choice]: In the future, check your clients.
V [choice]: Clear, won’t happen again.
V [choice]: The girl deserved another chance.
V [choice]: Potent metaphor. Cook it up yourself?
Mr. Hands: I’m an old hand in this game, V.
Mr. Hands: Perhaps, perhaps not. Spare yourself the mental effort.

title: The Brazilian Job
text:
Mr. Hands: Gig objective: Find Mark Bana

Location: Longshore Stacks

Details: The powers that be love wrestling in the mud of our little Dogtown swamp. But let’s not fool ourselves - what would Dogtown be without its incomprehensible spy games and power struggles? I suppose the answer’s not worth our efforts.

In any case, I’ve received word from some Brazilian intelligence agents. They’ve lost someone in Dogtown and would like to find him. The lost soul’s name: Mark Bana. Now, if there’s secret agents, surely there must be a catch? I’ve found one, though there may be others for you to find yourself. The known unknown: the agents seek their colleague without the knowledge or approval of the Brazilian Intelligence Agency. I suggest you ask them why. Oh, and have fun.
Mr. Hands: I hear birds chirping of Bana. No, they won’t quiet it now – our Brazilian duo is bound for trouble. Contract closed, V.
Mr. Hands: Destroying the biomonitor was the correct decision. Caution over bravura, V, as I always say. Your funds are on their way, the contract closed.
V [choice]: Caution? More like bein’ pragmatic.
V [choice]: Gettin’ pretty good at sweepin’ shit under the rug, huh?
V [choice]: Guess I got a soft spot for chooms who actually believe in something. Had to give her the biomon.
V [choice]: Wasn’t my decision to make – biomon’s their biz, not mine.
Mr. Hands: Ah, but what’s in a name, V? All’s well that ends well – for us at least. Until our next contract.
Mr. Hands: Ah, so you wash your hands of the matter? Leaving others to bathe theirs in blood. I won’t stoop so low as to judge; I hate to be bored, just like you. Still, I do pity our agents. Until our next contract, V.

title: Treating symptoms
text:
Mr. Hands: Gig objective: Eliminate Milko Alexis

Location: Voodoo Boys base at the spa in Luxor Heights

Details: Indira Barazza wouldn’t be the first or the last to fall prey to the Voodoo Boys’ blackmail. What’s interesting is the gang seems to have only the technical employees of her corp in their sights. They made our client an offer she couldn’t refuse – cooperate or die. Indira chose a third route: call me. The Voodoo Boy threatening to hack her lungs is one Milko Alexis. See to it that he kindly leaves her the fuck alone.
Mr. Hands: Short and sweet, V. Just the way I like it. Our client can breathe easy once more – unlike Milko. I'm transferring the funds as we speak; your work here is done.
Mr. Hands: NetWatch contacted me. They've put Indira under witness protection; she'll have a full netrunner guard 24/7. They really couldn't praise you enough, V. It is good to have friends in corporate places, even in Dogtown. That is, especially in Dogtown. Your well-deserved funds are on their way, and your gig is complete.
V [choice]: NetWatch owes you one now. So I think you owe me a little extra.
V [choice]: Don’t like surprises on the job. So you didn’t know NetWatch was sniffing around, or did you just not bother to tell me?
V [choice]: Had to wipe a whole robot army. Coulda warned me the Voodoo Boys were out there playing build-a-bot.
V [choice]: Not short or sweet. Expect a call from NetWatch. The suits were also sniffing around... Milko’s sudden death foiled their plans.
Mr. Hands: I don’t tip. On principle.
Mr. Hands: If you think I’ll raise your rate accordingly, think again.
Mr. Hands: And I prefer not to employ those who are easily surprised. Something for you to consider.
Mr. Hands: They’ll sniff out nothing. Not on me, at least - you I assume they caught red-handed. But, well, if you’re not on the run from NetWatch, are you really living?

Mr. Hands: Gig objective: Extract NCPD officers from Dodger’s base

Location: Pacifica, former NCPD station

Details: V, we have two officers in need. Somehow – and don’t ask me how – they landed in the base of one of Hansen’s men. Dodger, to be exact. Until recently, this “base” was a functioning NCPD station.

Two cops held prisoner in their old station-turned-drug drop? Absurd, yes, but what can I say? That’s life, particularly in Dogtown. Before you charge in there, go and talk to our client, Stella. The poor thing’s engaged to one of these two super troopers.

You won’t leave our boys in blue hanging, will you, V?

title: Scavengers in the Clinic
text:
Mr. Hands: Gig objective: Rescue Anthony Anderson

Location: Haven Clinic on Montaña de Oro Ave

Details: The poor never catch a break, do they? Anderson’s clinic can barely make ends meet, and now the Scavengers are giving them hell, too. The gang has some business with the good doctor – and he couldn’t care less. He’s barricaded himself in his office; nobody in, nobody out. What’s worse, Anderson’s the only physician the clinic has. Please, speak with his assistant Odell Blanco at the scene and get this sick situation sorted.
Mr. Hands: You're the cure to all my ills, V. But that's enough praise for now – let’s not have you raising your rates. Your payment is on its way, the gig closed.
Mr. Hands: I heard the news about Anderson. Well, even the best hands slip on occasion. The important thing is, you've removed the scavengers and the patients may now return. I may not be a man of faith, but I do believe in Odell – no, he's certainly not one to leave his flock.
V [choice]: Money isn’t everything, Hands. Those people needed help. Sometimes kindness pays, y’know?
V [choice]: Pleasure’s all mine, Hands.

messages.text:
Gig objective: Rescue Anthony Anderson

Location: Haven Clinic on Montaña de Oro Ave

Details: The poor never catch a break, do they? Anderson’s clinic can barely make ends meet, and now the Scavengers are giving them hell, too. The gang has some business with the good doctor – and he couldn’t care less. He’s barricaded himself in his office; nobody in, nobody out. What’s worse, Anderson’s the only physician the clinic has. Please, speak with his assistant Odell Blanco at the scene and get this sick situation sorted.
You're the cure to all my ills, V. But that's enough praise for now – let’s not have you raising your rates. Your payment is on its way, the gig closed.

title: Massacre at the Longshore Stacks
text:
Mr. Hands: Gig objective: Neutralize Leon Rinder

Location: Longshore Stacks

Details: We’ve got a situation in the Longshore Stacks. The mess was made by Leon Rinder, once a soldier with Hansen, now killer of eight. It remains unclear what Rinder was doing in the Stacks, what caused him to snap, or why he left Hansen’s ranks. So many questions, V, so few answers. One thing is certain: the victims’ families want to get their hands on Rinder. But first, we need to find him. Enter you, V.

Go to the Stacks, search the area and talk to their unofficial representative, Briana Dolson. Maybe you’ll find a lead.
Mr. Hands: You delivered Rinder’s dog tag, well done. Contract closed. Out of curiosity, though... wherever did you find Hansen’s former friend?
V [choice]: Scavside. Weirdly enough, they helped him... choom was trying to offload his chrome, get the fuck outta Dtown.
V [choice]: In Pacifica. Wasn’t in the best of shape... choom practically neutralized himself.
Mr. Hands: Well, well, and they say there’s no reasonable people in BARGHEST. Relatively reasonable. One point to Rinder for trying to leave... but minus fifteen for going to the scavengers for help.
Mr. Hands: Pure professionalism, served ice cold. Just as it should be. Thank you, V.

title: Regarding the prototype
text:
Mr. Hands: Gig objective: Retrieve a prototype implant and its schematics

Location: Construction site, the Scraper, Longshore Stacks

Details: A few days ago the scavengers raided a convoy returning from the stadium. Soon after, I received a call from the regional director of Zetatech informing me said convoy was theirs. Now, they’d tried to keep their transaction on the down low - unfortunately, it seems the scavs go lower.  Zetatech lost a valuable prototype implant along with its technical documentation. They’d like to retrieve their lost items. Fortunately, the prototype is emitting a trackable signal.

It’s pointed us to a scav haunt in the Longshore Stacks, at the construction site of a long-unfinished skyscraper. I’ve sent you the coordinates; I trust you’ll do the rest.
Mr. Hands: V. A little birdie chirped that you retrieved Zetatech's paraphernalia. Any issues along the way?
Mr. Hands: A little birdie chirped that you only managed to procure the schematics, yet the prototype was left with the hostage you rescued? Care to elaborate?
Mr. Hands: V, I received word Hasan, your acquaintance from the Scraper, wishes to contact you. Naturally, I declined to hand him your contact details. However, if you wish to speak to him, I've sent you his current coordinates.
Mr. Hands: V, I received word someone attempted to sell a Zetatech ocular implant in Dogtown. Bells ring, buzzers buzz. I trust I needn't point out the similarities between said prototype and the one you sought among the scavengers. The very same, perhaps?
Mr. Hands: My people will handle the rest.
You really have a knack for solving complicated situations, V.
V [choice]: You two still in touch? Wouldn’t think you’d have much to talk about.
V [choice]: Hasan? That choom spells trouble.
V [choice]: Thanks. How’s the hostage?
V [choice]: One thing’s still botherin’ me... maybe we could help that hostage somehow?
V [choice]: What can I say, it’s a gift. How’s the hostage?
V [choice]: Thanks. For the favor too.
V [choice]: Nothin’ much. Rescued a Zetatech suit, choom slotted the prototype. Said he’d find his way back.
V [choice]: Name’s Hasan, Zetatech suit. He didn’t contact you?
V [choice]: Nope. Birdie missed that bit?
V [choice]: Nope. All in the drop point.
V [choice]: Maybe, maybe not. I’ll check it out.
V [choice]: Thought we closed that contract.
Mr. Hands: He’ll go to Zetatech, as we agreed. I doubt you’ll be seeing any more of him. However, you will be seeing your payment shortly.
Mr. Hands: My people will handle the rest.
You really have a knack for solving complicated situations, V.
Mr. Hands: What hostage, V? All who were in that convoy perished in the scavenger ambush, end of story. Your payment is on its way.
Mr. Hands: He’ll walk free, as we agreed. Your payment is on its way.
Mr. Hands: Ah, it was nothing. I appreciated your call. Your funds will arrive any moment.
Mr. Hands: Color me shocked – he did no such thing. Zetatech will not be thrilled, but I suppose that’s my cross to bear. However, I dare say you could have informed me earlier, V. At least you secured the schematics – contract closed.
Mr. Hands: He did not. We will have to make do with the schematics. The contract is closed – but next time, V, I would appreciate hearing from you directly.
Mr. Hands: I suppose I wished to hear it from the horse’s mouth. Your payment should arrive soon.
Mr. Hands: I commend your work, V. Your payment is on its way.
Mr. Hands: Merely the debt of gratitude he owes us both. You’ll find him in the Longshore Stacks.
Mr. Hands: An amusing remark coming from you, V. In any case, you’ll find him in the Longshore Stacks.
Mr. Hands: A fact of which I’m well aware. How wonderful I needn’t even ask for such favors to be done. He was last seen in a derelict building on Elizabeth Kress Street.
Mr. Hands: We did. Yet it might still interest you to learn he was last seen in a Golden Pacific squat.
Mr. Hands: V. A little birdie chirped that you retrieved Zetatech's paraphernalia. Any issues along the way?
V [choice]: Couldn't find the prototype. Got the schematics, though. That a problem?
V [choice]: Got there too late, scavs must've moved the prototype. Only found the schematics.
Mr. Hands: It’s certainly a snag. Zetatech will not be thrilled, though I suppose that’s my cross to bear. Your payment is on its way, V.
Mr. Hands: If they had, I would have heard. Knowing those savages, they either damaged it beyond repair or simply tossed it in the incinerator. At least you managed to secure the schematics. Your payment is on its way.

title: Kidnapping - Lina Malina
text:
Mr. Hands: An interesting item of business has fallen into my lap, V. Lina Malina, a local BD celebrity, claims she’s been kidnapped and is currently being held against her will in a BD rental studio called Brainporium. Lina seeks a merc who will free her from her captor’s clutches.
All in all, it would be a credible, solid assignment, were it not for the fact that I failed to confirm the client’s identity. The data I received from her is at odds in several places with what my trusted sources tell me; as such, I will not be playing middleman in this matter.
However, should you be so inclined, I’ve sent the coordinates she relayed to me. I, meanwhile, will do as the Romans do and wash my hands of the matter.
V [choice]: Lina Malina? Sounds familiar... think I saw a poster or something?
V [choice]: Lina who? Never heard of her. Usually stick to the mindfulness BDs. Been real into scop-grilling competitions too – now that's what I call entertainment.
Mr. Hands: I can’t say I’ve been following her career, if one can call it such. Yet, as always, I aim to keep my finger on the pulse of things.
Mr. Hands: Well, She’s a braindance star who records controversial footage with her scavenger entourage. The scrolls feature parties and firefights; rather unimaginative material, if you ask me.
V [choice]: Turns out Lina Malina didn’t hire you, but she was still involved. Long story short, gave her a new sister and both are very happy. Ah, days like this remind me why I got into mercwork in the first place.
V [choice]: So your captive – Edgar Tool. A freak BD wreath accident had him thinking he was Lina Malina. Managed to convince him he was actually her long-lost sister. Anyway, scrolled a little BD together, turned out pretty great if you ask me.
V [choice]: Dunno if it was worth getting involved. Turns out the client was a BD rental owner, goes by Tool. Choom had a psychotic break and thought he was Lina... anyway, now he doesn’t, but I might’ve accidentally given him some sort of persecution complex.
V [choice]: Turns out it wasn’t Lina, but some choom called Tool. Had a BD accident, started thinking he was Lina. Set him free, now he just thinks he’s an FIA clone.
V [choice]: Gig called for a psychiatrist, not a merc. Choom got stuck thinking he was someone else. Thankfully managed to help him, now he’s back to his old self.
V [choice]: See why you had your doubts. Client wasn’t Lina Malina, but the co-owner of Brainporium, Edgar Tool. Guy had a freak BD wreath accident, thought he was a BD star. Thankfully managed to convince him otherwise.
V [choice]: Easy peasy. Freed the client, gig complete.
V [choice]: Yeah, that wasn’t Lina Malina, just some choom called Tool. Guy was locked up, I set him free, so the gig’s in the bag.
V [choice]: Well that was one big waste of time. Not even worth writing what happened.
V [choice]: No surprise you didn’t wanna get involved in that dumb mess. BD rental store owner thought he was Lina Malina, so the co-owner locked him in the basement. No helping those two.
Mr. Hands: Do you expect me to commend you on your failure? Return to work, please.
Mr. Hands: My, a wealth of information that I neither need nor desire. Return to work, please.
Mr. Hands: I see. Would you like a pat on the back? A 21-gun salute? Well, you can have my mildest congratulations. Now kindly return to work.
V [choice]: So the client wasn’t Lina, that’s for sure. Choom’s name was Tool, owns a BD rental place. His biz partner had him locked up in the basement, so I set him free. Got a kiss for my efforts... unsure how to feel about that.
V [choice]: Easy peasy. Freed the client, gig complete.
V [choice]: Not sure what’s going on with Lina Malina, but in this case some psychopath was holding his friend hostage in a BD booth. Killed the psycho, freed the prisoner.
V [choice]: Turns out your “Lina” was some choom being held in the basement by his biz partner. Wiped the partner, let the poor choom run free.

text:

Objective: Bring down propaganda machine slandering Weldon Holt

title: Dirt on Stove
text:
Muamar "El Capitan" Reyes: Gig type: Thievery
Objective: Steal documents incriminating Matheus Stove
Location: Kendachi Factory, El Camino Rd
Details:

Your mom ever tell you saying "two wrongs don't make a right"? Yeah, well we're the third one.
Kendachi's about to select a new director of some shit department or other – that part doesn't matter. What's important is it's two candidates for one gig. Know where this is going, right? Bingo – one of 'em is my client and he wants dirt on his new arch-nemesis Matheus Stove.

Main problem is that Stove's the human equivalent of unseasoned, boiled scop. He's bland, he's boring. No bodies in his backyard, no dates with minors, nothing. But there's no way a guy in his position in a place like Night City is 100% dirt-free. I mean there's no fuckin' way.

Couple contacts of mine say Stove has a few strings tied to the Valentinos. You need to slip into his office and slip a few files off his computer. If we're lucky, we get something to back up the rumors, costing Mr. Squeaky-clean Stove his shot at the promotion.

Main problem is that Stove's the human equivalent of unseasoned, boiled scop. He's bland, he's boring. No bodies in his backyard, no dates with minors, nothing. But there's no way a guy in his position in a place like Night City is 100% dirt-free. I mean there's no fuckin' way.

Couple contacts of mine say Stove has a few strings tied to the Valentinos. You need to slip into his office and slip a few files off his computer. If we're lucky, we get something to back up the rumors, costing Mr. Squeaky-clean Stove his shot at the promotion.
Received. Job's done – get outta there.
Beautiful work, V. Stove's finished even if he don't know it yet. Big thanks. Contract's closed and the eddies're flyin' at ya.

title: Doing humanity a favor
text:

Target: Logan Garcia
Location: Old Paint Factory on Baptiste St.
Details:

Target's name is one Logan Garcia. He runs an Animals fight club. Used to fight himself, actually. Still gets in the ring from time to time. Problem is he doesn't know when to put on the brakes. Recently he knocked his sparring buddy, Lenny Steiner, to the mat with a giant dent in his skull. Except instead of calling for help, he had the kid thrown in the bay with a cinderblock tied round his neck.

title: Beta Acid
text:
Muamar "El Capitan" Reyes: Gig type: Search and Recover
Objective: Retrieve a container containing beta acid
Location: Dewdrop Inn
Details:

This ain't too complicated, you know the drill. Something slipped through somebody's fingers and it's your job to get it back. Got this choom, Doug – Denver Doug – a ripper. Recently did this patch job on a 6th street dickhole and when he took off Denver noticed a gallon of beta acid gone missing. Dunno wtf he uses it for but that 6er knows all kinds of shit can get cooked from it on the street. 1+1 = a dealer klepped it.

So Denver hired a guy, Booker Updike, to find the missing acid, then POOF – he's a ghost. Last seen at the Dewdrop Inn in Arroyo. Head over there, get your hands on that beta, and if you got a minute, find out what happened to this Booker guy.
V [choice]: Found him. He's dead – poisoned. Accident, by the looks of it.
V [choice]: Couldn't find him anywhere
Muamar "El Capitan" Reyes: So, V, the beta acid's secure? Padrísimo. And I'm puttin' you down for ten bonus points for solvin' the mystery of Booker's fate. It's clean work, V. Contract's closed, gratitude's on the way.
Muamar "El Capitan" Reyes: Well, I have the beta acid, but still got no clue what happened with Booker. Expected more from you, V. Closing this one and filing it under "Meh..."

title: One flew over the cuckoo's nest
text:
Muamar "El Capitan" Reyes: Gig type: SOS: Merc Needed
Objective: Jasmine Dixon
Location: Psychiatric ward on Sequoia St.
Details:

I'm not a fan of badges. They stick their nose in other people's biz, give ordinary people a hard time, do the corps' bidding. But sometimes it's worth getting into bed with your enemies – at least they'll owe you something for later.

There's this badge, Jasmine Dixon. She's been patrolling NC streets since '61, reached the rank of sergeant. One day at the precinct she heard something she shouldn't've. Instead of keeping her mouth shut, she took it to her supervisor. The next day they wheeled her off to a psych ward. The kind where they prescribe lobotomies and electrotherapy.

Her husband will do anything to help her and as far as payment goes, "anything" is as good as it gets. You'll get your standard rate, of course. So, whaddya say? Gotta help a couple in need, don't you think?
Muamar "El Capitan" Reyes: Understood. Car's headin your way.
Muamar "El Capitan" Reyes: V, you were supposed to get Jasmine to the ride. The chick's in shock – she doesn't know up from down! What if she made a wrong turn or-- Look, you're lucky she made it, OK?
Muamar "El Capitan" Reyes: Solid work, V. Jasmine's on her way to her dearest husband. Shit, think I might even cry. Job well done, V. Closing the gig.

title: Security escort needed
text:
Muamar "El Capitan" Reyes: Gig type: SOS: Merc Needed
Objective: Rescue Flavio dos Santos
Location: Mallagra St.
Details:

6th Street got shaken up with an internal coup, the boss took a bullet in the back of the head. The guy who filled his shoes was the same who pulled the trigger – they call him Gunner.  The new bossman has unleashed a purge to rid the gang of all the people loyal to the last chief. My client, Flavio, is next in line to get shot and he'd very much like to skip town.

Already struck a deal with the nomads who agreed to ship him to the other coast. All you have to do is escort Flavio to the place their guide will pick him up. Little problem to note: there's already a price on our friend's head, so he's gotta watch it.

Sending you coords of where Flavio's holed up. You need to get there, load him into your ride, and deliver to the nomads ASAP. Keep your iron at the ready and don't forget to always check your mirrors. 6th St gave him a death sentence so any tails on his ass are likely to be hot.
Muamar "El Capitan" Reyes: Not good, V. Not good at all. Flavio's worm-chow and what's worse – my street cred took a hit. And you know there's nothing worth more to a fixer than their cred. I'm not the vindictive type, so I'll let this slide. But I've got a good memory – consider this strike one. Next time better be a home run.
Muamar "El Capitan" Reyes: Now that's what I call pro mercwork! Flavio's yappin' my ears off, says he's never met anyone tougher than you. Bet it's gonna stay that way for a while. Rare breed – mercs like you. Contract's closed, already flicked the eds your way.
Muamar "El Capitan" Reyes: Expect some company, V. The grumpy variety. 6th Street got wise and learned you helped Flavio outta NC, along with sending some of their chooms to the pearly gates. Maybe you better move too. Not out of NC of course, just outta their crosshairs.

title: Bit of charity
text:
Muamar "El Capitan" Reyes: Gig type: Thievery
Objective: Steal an automated Zetatech vehicle
Location: Motel on Wollesen St.
Details:

Better get some tissues ready – this one's gonna be a real tearjerker. Pedro Aimar, a guy who thinks he's some kinda nova netrunner cuz he coded a few algorithms for Zetatech. Well, now he wants to klep their ass. It's not what you think – see, he has some kinda health problems and Zetatech doesn't wanna chip in for his operation. Crazy, right? A corp that doesn't give a shit about its employee. I'm practically speechless. Well, now look at that... tears are splashing onto my screen. This is a life and death situation, V! Pedro needs our help! He (and we) reeeaally need the eddies!

Pedro wants to klep a Zetatech truck full of A-grade tech (already got a buyer). Meet up with Pedro and figure out how you wanna play this. If you help him, our readiness to help a poor soul in need will be handsomely rewarded.
Muamar "El Capitan" Reyes: Well, well! Got ourselves a real edgerunner, huh? You lunatic! Waitin' and baitin' the corpos like that! Hah! I fucking love it! 'K, back to biz. Pedro's happy, so we're golden. Eddies flowing to your account now. Gig's closed.
Muamar "El Capitan" Reyes: Beautifully done, V. Dunno about Pedro, but I consider you my hero already. See, V? Play your cards right, you'll always walk away with full pockets. Closing the gig.
Muamar "El Capitan" Reyes: Jesus, V, what a shitshow! The gig, the client, the eddies, V! Down the drain – all of it! Don't even get me started on the wheels! Just... grrr!

title: Listening in on Kendachi
text:
Muamar "El Capitan" Reyes: Gig type: Agent Saboteur
Objective: Deliver van
Location: Kendachi Factory, Arroyo
Details:

You ever watch the news? Personally, I think it's all propaganda. But that's just me. Still, people watch, and some people make the news.

My client's Ted Fox, an N54 reporter. He's doing a story on the link between gangs and corps. On paper, they're enemies, but in reality, seems like the corporats and gangoons are scratching each other's backs. Key word – seems. Ted needs hard evidence.

That's where you come in to save the day. Ted'll tell you exactly what you have to do, but be ready to get onto Kendachi factory grounds, poke around. All clear? Head on over to Ted. As they say in the media biz – it's showtime!
Muamar "El Capitan" Reyes: Preem work. Ted's gonna shit so hard on those Kendachi fucks. They won't know what hit 'em. Anyways, respect for running a tip-top op. Closing the contract and releasing your eddies.
Muamar "El Capitan" Reyes: Gig's done. Ted's got all the dirt on Kendachi he needs. That said, V... I gotta give you a C minus for effort. Closin' the contract, but I can't say I'm happy about it.
Muamar "El Capitan" Reyes: Humor me for a sec... How do you plant a bug under a truck that you blew to pieces, hm? Oh, that's right – you don't! What the hell's gotten into you, V?! Someone pinch me 'cause I must be dreamin' – I mean, who pulls this kinda shit?!

title: Rihanna's severance
text:
Muamar "El Capitan" Reyes: Gig type: Thievery
Objective: Retrieve Rihanna Kumar's Cytech research
Location: Cytech Factory on Olivia St.
Details:

Rihanna Kumar used to be a top engineer at Cytech. Lived in a preem house, ate ganic meat, looked down on the poor – all the corpo basics. Then her little fairy tale took a twist. Cytech turned her world upside down. No more house, no more meat – but got new perspective on poverty from the other side of the fence. She's enlisted us to help her get a severance package.

Break into the Cytech factory and retrieve the data of the projects our poor, mistreated client was working on. With that, she can turn this personal shitstorm into a new dawn for her career (fuck... missed my calling as a poet). Anyway, most important thing is that she's paying us for the gig. Have fun.
Muamar "El Capitan" Reyes: Heh, y'know, it's after gigs like this I think to myself, "Shit, am I glad I got V." Keep up the preem work. Closing the gig.
Muamar "El Capitan" Reyes: Data received, thanks. Now make yourself scarce

title: Viruses 101
text:
Muamar "El Capitan" Reyes: Gig type: Agent Saboteur
Objective: Infect 6th Street computer with a virus
Location: 6th Street hideout on MLK Blvd
Details:

Those boys and girls from 6th Street think they got wicked smarts, that they can jump a Militech transport in my hood without me knowing about it. They think they can crack corpo weapons and tip the balance of power in this city to their favor. It's time they got a rude awakening.

I'll snap you the location of the 6th St hideout and the door code. Job's simple – find a way in, look for the comp they use to jailbreak corpo tech, upload the virus I'll supply to you and voila, their fancy new weapon melts into a sparkly new slagheap.

One more thing. If you happen to find a Lucius Thoran, do me a favor and make his ass disappear, will ya? Thoran's a techie – came up with this gonk plan, which makes him a real thorn in my ass. Pun intended.

Stay safe and have fun.
Muamar "El Capitan" Reyes: Profesh as ever, V! Sixers'll think twice before sliding their gonk asses anywhere near my turf again. And that thing with Lucius Thoran? Hm-hm-hm! Cherry on top! Contract ca-losed!
Muamar "El Capitan" Reyes: Looks like the Sixers learned their lesson... Can't say the same for our lucky choom, Lucius Thoran. But hey, guess I can't complain, right? Job's done, matter's resolved. Just, y'know, try to go that extra mile next time, 'K?

Muamar "El Capitan" Reyes: Damn, that was weak. I need your A-game, not your D-game, all right? Maybe head down to the ripper's or something, get your ass into shape.
Muamar "El Capitan" Reyes: Been hearing a lot about you, V. People know they're dealing with a serious merc, not some Afterlife wannabe. You'll be seeing some fresh items under the counter, better prices too. See? Now everyone wants to do biz with V! ;)
Muamar "El Capitan" Reyes: Boy is your name making the rounds. Just so happens respect on the street is a valuable thing. In the long run, what matters is who you know and who's worth doin' biz with.
